commit.message:
8387311: [Lilliput2] ArrayKlass::hash_offset_in_bytes overflows int for ~2GB+ arrays

With -XX:+UseCompactObjectHeaders an array's identity hash is stored in a
hidden word the GC appends after the elements when it expands a hashed-but-not-
expanded object. ArrayKlass::hash_offset_in_bytes computed that offset as
base_offset + (length << log2_element_size) in 32-bit int. For a multi-byte
element array of ~2GB or more the shift overflows to a negative value, and
oopDesc::initialize_hash_if_necessary then writes the 4-byte hash at a sign-
extended negative displacement from the object base. That write lands outside
the array, crashing with SIGSEGV or silently corrupting a neighboring heap
object during GC relocation.

Compute the hash offset in 64-bit and thread it through as size_t. The hash
slot of a large array can legitimately sit beyond INT_MAX, so the few hash
read/write sites address it with new size_t-offset accessors
oopDesc::hash_field / hash_field_put. The field-access API itself is unchanged.
InstanceKlass and mirror offsets always fit an int, and the C2 side
(ciInstanceKlass) checked_casts back to int.

Adds gc/stress/ihash/TestHashCodeLargeArray.java which hashes a 2GB+ long[],
forces relocating GCs across Parallel/Serial/G1/Shenandoah/Z, and verifies the
hash and contents survive (crashes on the unfixed VM, passes after the fix).
